paragraphs: My name is Tom, and I am twelve years old. Our class had a play on Friday. The play was about a rich king in a cold land. Ben and I play chess at lunch, so I know how a king looks. I was the king in the play. My diary had the plan for my mask. "Make an enormous white mustache," I wrote. Here is how to make a king mask. You need a white paper plate, white cotton, and glue. You also need scissors, a black pen, a yellow pen, and a string.

Step one: Cut two holes for the eyes in the plate. Step two: Draw a yellow crown above the holes. Step three: Draw a black line for each eyebrow. Step four: Glue the white cotton under the holes. Now the cotton is your mustache. Ben looked at my mask and laughed. "It is enormous!" he said. "A king needs an enormous mustache," I said.

Step five: Make a small hole on each side of the plate. Step six: Put a string in each hole. Then tie the string behind your head. In the play, the cold king came on a sledge. Our sledge was a big box with white paper snow. Hugo pulled the sledge, and I sat in the box. "Is the mask too big?" asked Hugo. "No, I can see you well," I said.

On Friday, the class watched our play. At the end, the rich king gave his gold coins to the village. Everyone clapped. That night, I wrote in my diary. "The king was kind, and the mustache was great." Ben still wants to play chess with the king. I smiled and took off the mask.
